name: Code comments by the writing guide

pr.title: Write code comments and docstrings by the writing guide
pr.head: a4295a21db3f4d973f52937f0ce0437dc146aa47

summary: Projector's skills share two rule documents. The code guidelines, skills/guidelines.md, say what code any skill writes must follow, and the review flags a break of them as a finding. The writing guide, skills/writing.md, says how every skill writes prose for people, such as plans, reviews, and commit messages.

Until this change, the code guidelines said only when code needs a comment, and the writing guide did not cover comments at all. So an agent that wrote a comment had no rule for how to word it, and comments came out recounting the change that made them, such as "changed to use a timer as the review suggested".

This pull request adds § 12 to the writing guide, on code comments and docstrings, and makes guidelines.md § 1 require it. Each skill that writes or judges code then points at § 12: implement and fix-pr write comments by it, the review reads comments against it and cites it in a finding, and write routes a comment request to it. The change is instruction text only; no Python or TypeScript changes.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Written-rules pass: the part of the review method that reads a change against the rules written down in guidelines.md and the repository's own documents.
  • P2 finding: a review thread that blocks the pull request, used for a bounded defect or a break of a written rule.
  • § 11: the writing guide's section that keeps a change's history in the commit log rather than in the text, with an exception for history the reader still meets.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html:
• The first review found one P2: § 12's first bullet banned "the old behavior that the code replaced" with no exception, which conflicted with § 11's exception for history a reader still meets. The bullet now ends with that exception, and the latest review verified the fix and found nothing open.
  • The paragraphs the first review suggested rewrapping in writing.md and docs/plugins.md are rewrapped.

groups.title: The new rule and where it lives
groups.kicker: Writing guide § 12, and the code guidelines that make it binding
intro: The writing guide gains § 12. It says the rest of the guide applies to comments, except § 3 on document kinds and § 10 on pull requests, and it adds four rules: give the reason in the present tense, write for a maintainer who meets the code cold, open a docstring with what the caller gets, and keep the comment short and true. A before-and-after example closes the section.
guidelines.md § 1 then makes § 12 a written rule, the same way § 2 makes the testing guide one. A comment that breaks the writing guide becomes a P2 finding that cites the section it breaks.

checks.text: Because guidelines.md § 1 makes every break of § 12 a blocking finding, the wording of § 12 decides what reviews flag and what fix-pr deletes.

files.note: Adds § 12 on code comments and docstrings, and widens the intro's scope to name them.

checks.text: This sentence keeps § 11's exception: a comment may name an old behavior that a reader still meets, such as data an older release wrote, and say what the code does with it. Compatibility comments such as the one above FORMER_LABEL_COLORS in src/projector/review.py depend on it.
The citations § 2, § 3, § 8, § 10, and § 11 name the sections they describe at this head: § 8 lists "This function"-style filler, and § 11 covers history.

files.note: § 1 requires comments and docstrings to follow the writing guide, and says a break of it is a finding that cites its section.

groups.title: Skills that write or judge code
groups.kicker: Each skill points at § 12 in the step where it writes or reads a comment
intro: Each skill that writes or reviews code now names § 12 where it handles comments. implement writes each comment it keeps by § 12. fix-pr writes the comment a fix adds by § 12, never naming the finding. In review-pr, the written-rules pass reads changed comments against § 12, and the incremental review's prose check does too. write lists code comments in its description and routes them to § 12.

checks.text: Every skill that references writing.md was read at this head; rewrite, spec, summarize-pr, and cleanup need no change for the wider scope.

files.note: Tells the implementer to write each comment and docstring it keeps by § 12.
Tells a fix to write its comments by § 12, without naming the finding, the review, or the replaced code.
The written-rules pass reads § 12 when a change adds or edits a comment, and gives writing.md § 12 as a citation.
The incremental review's prose check reads comments against § 12 and treats a comment that tells history as a finding.
Names code comments and docstrings in the description, and sends them to § 12.

groups.title: Plugin documentation
groups.kicker: The user-facing description of the shared guides
intro: docs/plugins.md says that the writing guide covers comments in the code a skill changes, and that a review flags a comment that breaks it.

files.note: Adds comments and docstrings to the writing guide's scope.
